title: Derivation and long-term expansion of human endometrial and decidual organoids.
protocol: Transfer tissue samples into basic wash medium plus penicillin/streptomycin at room temperature.
Examine tissues macroscopically and discard non-decidual tissue.
Select only tissue pieces larger than 1 cm³ which can be confidently identified as decidua compacta or decidua spongiosa.
Wash the selected tissue in basic culture medium with gentle stirring for 20 min to remove contaminating blood.
Transfer tissue pieces with forceps to a clean dish and mince with scalpels to 0.5-1 mm³ pieces.
Transfer minced tissue to a 60 mL lidded, disposable container of sufficient diameter to allow mixing by agitation.
Add 10 -30 ml warmed collagenase/dispase solution.
Place the container in a heated shaker at 37°C with gentle shaking to digest.
Sample the digest after 20 min and subsequently at 10-min intervals to check for free glandular elements.
Dilute the enzyme/tissue mix with RPMI-1640 medium when glands are abundant to minimize further disaggregation.
Transfer to a larger container if necessary.
Swirl the container firmly but do not shake.
Leave to stand for 2 min to allow undigested tissue fragments to sediment.
Pass the supernatant through one or more 100 µm cell sieves.
Wash the supernatant through well with RPMI-1640 medium.
Invert the sieves over a petri dish and backwash the glandular elements from the membrane by forceful pipetting using a plastic Pasteur pipette.
Transfer the backwashed glands to a universal tube and pellet by centrifugation at 500g for 5 min.
Re-suspend glandular elements in 1-2 ml Advanced DMEM/F12 medium.
Gently pipette up and down several times to partially dissociate cells.
Transfer the suspension to 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes and pellet by centrifugation.
Remove the supernatant and estimate the volume of the pellet.
Flick the tube to loosen the pellet and place on ice for 2-3 min.
Add 20 x volume:volume of ice-cold Matrigel and pipette gently to mix.
Place the tube back onto ice immediately.
Plate 20-25 μl drops of Matrigel/cell suspension into the center of wells of Corning 48-well tissue culture plates.
Place the plates in the incubator to set for 15 min.
Overlay each drop with 250 μl Expansion Medium.
Examine cultures for the appearance of hollow spheroids, replacing the expansion medium every 2-3 days.
Scrape backwards and forwards across the growth surface of each well to detach the Matrigel drop into the medium using a 1ml pipette tip.
Transfer the contents of the wells into 1.5mL microcentrifuge tubes at a ratio of 4 wells per tube.
Centrifuge at 600g for 6 min to pellet.
Remove the supernatant and add approximately 150μL Advanced DMEM F12 to each tube.
Pipette up and down 300 times through a small bore pipette tip to break up the organoids and the Matrigel.
Add 1ml Advanced DMEM F12 and centrifuge at 600g for 6 min.
Remove supernatant, add 150 uL Advanced DMEM F12, and pipette up and down manually a further 80 times using moderate force.
Add 1ml Advanced DMEM F12 and centrifuge at 600g for 6 min.
Remove supernatant. The pellet should contain very little Matrigel.
If Matrigel is still present, estimate the volume and flick the tubes to re-suspend the pellets.
Place tubes on ice.
Add ice-cold Matrigel, mix gently, and replace the tube on ice.
Allow 20-25 µL Matrigel per well to be plated, minus any estimated residual Matrigel in the pellet.
Pool organoids together and mix gently to distribute them evenly throughout the Matrigel.
Dispense 20-25 µL drops carefully onto the centre of the growth area of wells in a 48-well culture plate, avoiding bubbles.
Place the culture plate in the incubator for 15 min to allow Matrigel to set.
Add 250 µL expansion medium to each well.
Replace medium every 2-3 days as appropriate.
Passage cells every 7-10 days as needed.
Remove culture medium from the wells.
Replace with 250 µL Cell Recovery Solution and place the plate on ice for 60 min.
Pool contents of wells into low-binding Eppendorf tubes using low-retention pipette tips.
Centrifuge at 600g for 6 min to pellet organoids.
Remove supernatant and add 200 µL Advanced DMEM F12 to each tube.
Manually pipette gently up and down 80 times with moderate force to partially disrupt organoids.
Add 1 mL Advanced DMEM F12 and centrifuge again.
Remove supernatant and flick pellets to re-suspend.
Place on ice.
Add 0.5-1 mL Recovery cell culture freezing medium to each tube with gentle mixing.
Transfer contents to labelled cryovials on ice.
Transfer immediately to ‘Mr. Frosty’ or similar cell freezing vessel at -80°C overnight, then to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage.
